name: iPhone
description: The iPhone (1st generation), announced in 2007, was Apple's first smartphone and marked the company's entry into the mobile phone market. It introduced a multi-touch interface and combined the functions of a mobile phone, iPod, and internet device.

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, Ambient light sensor

hardware: The original iPhone was powered by a Samsung S5L8900 processor based on the ARM11 architecture, running at approximately 412 MHz, and included 128 MB of RAM. It was sold in 4 GB and 8 GB configurations and later in a 16 GB option. The device contained a 1400 mAh lithium‑ion battery and included sensors such as an accelerometer, proximity sensor, and ambient light sensor. It supported GSM cellular networks but did not include 3G capability.
software: At launch, the iPhone ran iPhone OS 1, which featured applications such as Safari, Mail, Photos, Maps, YouTube, and iPod. The operating system used a touch-based interface with gestures like pinch-to-zoom. Native third-party applications were not supported initially; Apple instead promoted web applications accessed through the browser. The App Store was introduced in 2008 with iPhone OS 2, and the device was eventually upgradable to iPhone OS 3.1.3.
connectivity: The iPhone supported quad-band GSM and EDGE (2G) data networks, along with Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth 2.0. It did not include 3G cellular data, GPS, or MMS messaging at launch. Internet access was provided through the Safari browser, which rendered full desktop-style web pages.
camera: The device included a single 2‑megapixel rear camera designed for still photography. It did not support video recording, autofocus, flash, or a front-facing camera. Images could be viewed and managed through the Photos application and synchronized with a computer using iTunes.
release_and_reception: The iPhone was unveiled by Steve Jobs at Macworld 2007 and released later that year in the United States through an exclusive carrier agreement with AT&T. It initially retailed at $499 and $599 with a two-year contract, depending on storage capacity. Early reviews praised its touchscreen interface, web browsing experience, and design, while critics noted the lack of 3G connectivity, limited customization, and absence of third-party apps at launch.
impact: The original iPhone is widely regarded as one of the most influential consumer electronics devices of the 21st century. It helped popularize capacitive touchscreens, app-based software ecosystems, and the use of full web browsers on mobile phones. Its design approach—prioritizing a large touchscreen and minimal physical controls—became the dominant model for modern smartphones.
design: The original iPhone introduced a design that felt years ahead of its time. It featured a sleek aluminum back paired with a black plastic section at the bottom to allow radio signals to pass through — a necessary compromise that still looked intentional and premium. The front was dominated by a 3.5-inch display and was almost entirely free of buttons, apart from a single circular Home button. Its curved edges, slim profile, and minimalist layout reflected Apple's philosophy of simplicity and elegance.

name: iPhone 3G
description: The iPhone 3G, released on July 11, 2008, was the second generation of Apple's smartphone and the first to include 3G cellular connectivity. It retained many design elements of the original iPhone but introduced faster data transfer, GPS support, and the launch of the App Store, enabling third-party native applications for the first time.

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, Ambient light sensor, GPS

hardware: The iPhone 3G used the same Samsung S5L8900 ARM11 processor at 412 MHz as the original iPhone, with 128 MB of RAM. Storage options included 8 GB and 16 GB. It contained a 1150 mAh lithium‑ion battery and added GPS support. The device included the same basic sensors as the original iPhone and supported 3G HSDPA networks for faster mobile internet access.
software: The iPhone 3G launched with iPhone OS 2, introducing the App Store, which allowed users to download and install third-party native applications. It included built-in applications such as Safari, Mail, Maps, iPod, and YouTube. The operating system retained the multi-touch interface and gesture controls while adding enterprise features such as Microsoft Exchange support.
connectivity: The iPhone 3G supported quad-band GSM and tri-band 3G networks, Wi‑Fi, and Bluetooth 2.0. It included GPS for location services, enabling location-aware applications and navigation.
camera: The rear camera remained a single 2‑megapixel unit without video recording, autofocus, or flash. The iPhone 3G did not include a front-facing camera.
release_and_reception: Apple announced the iPhone 3G at the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) and released it on July 11, 2008, in multiple countries. Prices ranged from $199 for the 8 GB model to $299 for the 16 GB model with a two-year carrier contract. Reviews praised the faster 3G connectivity, GPS functionality, and App Store integration, though some critics called out battery life under heavy 3G usage.
impact: The iPhone 3G cemented Apple's role in the smartphone industry by introducing native apps via the App Store and improving location-based services. Its 3G connectivity and GPS capabilities set expectations for future smartphones and broadened mobile functionality.
design: The iPhone 3G featured a more rounded plastic back compared to the aluminum/plastic mix of the original iPhone, which improved signal reception for the new 3G capabilities. The front remained dominated by the 3.5-inch display with a single Home button below it. The device measured 115.5 × 62.1 × 12.3 mm and weighed 133 g. Physical controls included a sleep/wake button on top, volume buttons and mute switch on the left, and a recessed 3.5 mm headphone jack.

name: iPhone 3GS
description: The iPhone 3GS, announced in June 2009 and released in June 2009, was the third-generation iPhone. Building on the iPhone 3G, it offered improved performance, a higher-quality camera with video recording, and voice control. The 'S' stood for 'Speed', highlighting the device's faster processor and enhanced responsiveness.

specs.sensors: Accelerometer, Proximity sensor, Ambient light sensor, Digital compass

hardware: The iPhone 3GS introduced a faster 600 MHz ARM Cortex‑A8 processor and doubled RAM to 256 MB. Storage options included 8 GB, 16 GB, and 32 GB. The device featured a 1219 mAh lithium‑ion battery and included sensors such as an accelerometer, proximity sensor, ambient light sensor, and digital compass.
software: The iPhone 3GS launched with iPhone OS 3, introducing features such as copy and paste, video recording, and voice control. The App Store continued to expand, allowing users to download third-party apps. Later iOS updates brought additional functionality to supported devices.
connectivity: The iPhone 3GS supported quad-band GSM, tri-band 3G HSDPA networks, Wi‑Fi, and Bluetooth 2.1. GPS functionality enabled location-based services, navigation, and geotagging of photos.
camera: The rear camera was upgraded to 3 megapixels, added autofocus, and introduced video recording at 30 frames per second. The iPhone 3GS did not include a front-facing camera.
release_and_reception: The iPhone 3GS was unveiled at WWDC 2009 and released on June 19, 2009. The device was praised for its improved speed, enhanced camera, and new software features, though its exterior design remained similar to the iPhone 3G.
impact: The iPhone 3GS reinforced Apple's position in the smartphone market by combining hardware improvements with software enhancements. Features such as video recording, voice control, and a faster processor raised expectations for mobile devices and influenced subsequent iPhone designs.
design: The iPhone 3GS maintained the rounded plastic back and overall form factor of the iPhone 3G, measuring 115.5 × 62.1 × 12.3 mm and weighing 135 g. The front featured the same 3.5-inch display with a Home button below it. Minor design refinements improved scratch resistance and finish; physical buttons and ports remained unchanged.

name: iPhone 4
description: The iPhone 4 was announced by Apple on June 7, 2010, at the WWDC and released on June 24, 2010. it represented a major redesign of the iPhone lineup, introducing a new flat-edged industrial design and Apple's Retina Display. the device featured improved performance, a higher-resolution camera with HD video recording, and the introduction of a front-facing camera for video calls via FaceTime. it was the first iPhone to run iOS 4 at launch.

specs.rear-camera: 5 MP (LED flash, Tap to focus, HD video recording
specs.sensors: Gyroscope, Accelerometer, Digital compass, Proximity sensor

hardware: The iPhone 4 was powered by Apple's A4 system-on-chip, the same processor used in the first-generation iPad. it included 512 MB of RAM, doubling that of the iPhone 3GS. Storage options included 8 GB, 16 GB and 32 GB. The device featured a 5-megapixel rear camera with LED flash and support for 720p HD video recording at 30 frames per second. A VGA front-facing camera was introduced for video calls. It also included a gyroscope, adding enhanced motion sensing alongside the accelerometer, proximity sensor, and ambient light sensor.
software: The iPhone 4 launched with iOS 4, which introduced multitasking for supported applications, home screen folders, and a unified Mail inbox. it was the first iPhone to support FaceTime video calling over Wi-Fi. The device received long-term software support and was ultimately upgradable to iOS 7.1.2.
connectivity: The iPhone supported quad-band GSM and 3G HSDPA networks, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 2.1, and assited GPS. It continued to use the 30-pin dock conenctor for charging and data transfer. Shortly after release, some users reported signal attenuation issues when holding the device in a certain way, a controversy that became known as Antennagate. Apple later offered free bumper cases to address the issue.
camera: The iPhone 4 significantly improved camera capabilities compared to previous models. The 5-megapixel rear camera included autofocus, LED flash, tap-to-focus, and HD video recording at 720p. the introduction of a front-facing VGA cmaera enabled FaceTime video calls. The devoce also supported basic photo editing features within iOS.
release_and_reception: The iPhone 4 was unveiled on June 7, 2010, and released later that month in multiple countries. At launch, it was priced at $199 for the 16 GB model and $299 for the 32 GB model with a two-year contract. Reviews praised its high-resolution display, inproved cmaera, and refined design. However, early reception was affected by the antenna-related signal issues, which received widespread media attention.
impact: The iPhone 4 is widely regarded as one of Apple's most significant product redesigns. its retina display set a new standard for smartphone screen sharpness, and its glass-and-steel design influenced future iPhone generations. The introduction of FaceTime and improved camera capabilities helped define modern smartphone communication and photography.
design: The iPhone 4 introduced a new design featuring flat stainless steel edges and glass panels on both the front and back. the stainless steel frame also functioned as part of the antenna system. the device measured 115.2 x 58.6 x 9.3 mm and weighed 137 grams, making it thinner than previous models. The 3.5 inch display remained the same size but had significantly higher resolution. physical controls included the sleep/wake button on the top, volume buttons and mute switch on the left, and the 30 pin dock connector and speaker grille on the bottom. The device was available in black at launch, witha white version released later.
